title: Competitive Composability & Plugin Ecosystem Map for Enterprise Adoption
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Objective: Produce an operational map of competitor plugin/connectors ecosystems and a composability taxonomy that informs Redwood product bets for enterprise adoption (connectors, third-party plugins, vendor adapters, and partner tooling).

Background: Customers evaluating Redwood for production inference increasingly ask about integrations: vector DB connectors, knowledge-connector plugins, enterprise SSO/OAuth flows for third-party adapters, and vendor-specific deployment adapters (quantized binaries, CPU fallbacks). Current signal is fragmented: sales asks for compatibility matrices, SRE asks for supported auth patterns, and legal asks for licensing/contract risk heuristics.

Scope:
- Inventory top 12 model providers and 10 major connector/plugin ecosystems (vectors, RAG tooling, storage connectors, prompt management, commonsense toolkits).
- For each provider/ecosystem capture: auth model (API key, OAuth, service account), licensing constraints, latency profile, supported model flavors (float16/quantized/4-bit), on-prem vs hosted availability, failure/fallback behavior, and common integration patterns.
- Create a composability taxonomy describing integration friction types: auth mismatch, protocol mismatch, model flavor incompatibility, data residency/legal blockers, and operational observability gaps.
- Run automated synthetic probes (small benchmark harness) to capture latency and failure modes for representative flows (embed->vector-store->search->generate).
- Deliver artifacts: interactive spreadsheet, confluence use-case atlas, recommended product playbook with prioritized connector investments, and a small prototype dashboard spec for Console to display compatibility status per customer workspace.

Methodology:
1) Kickoff and stakeholder interviews (Sales, SRE, Legal, Solutions Eng).
2) Desk research and API spec harvesting from public docs + short developer signup where needed.
3) Automated probe harness (Python scripts + simple DAG) run against hosted test keys or public endpoints.
4) Qualitative validation calls with 6-8 enterprise buyers to validate impact vignettes and procurement triggers.
5) Consolidate into deliverables and present to GTM + Product Leadership for go/no-go on connector investments.

Risks & trade-offs:
- Some providers rate-limit test keys or block synthetic probes; fallback is manual sampling and partner outreach.
- Licensing/legal nuance may require Legal to triage; this will slow final recommendations for some connectors.
- Depth vs breadth trade-off: plan favors breadth for initial prioritization; we'll follow-up with deeper engineering runbooks for top-3 connectors if approved.

Success metrics:
- Coverage: matrix entries for at least 12 providers and 10 connector ecosystems.
- Product impact: a prioritized list of top 5 connector bets with expected revenue/retention uplift hypothesis.
- Engineering signal: prototype probe harness that can be reused for continuous monitoring (open-sourced in our infra repo).
acceptance_criteria: Interactive spreadsheet with per-connector fields (auth, license, model-flavor-support, observed latency, failure modes) published in Confluence
Consolidated recommendation deck with prioritized connector investments and buyer impact vignettes delivered to Product Leadership
Automated probe harness committed to infra repo with README and sample run logs
Stakeholder approvals: Sales, SRE, Legal, Solutions Engineering sign-off recorded as comments
